content: A functional murmur, also referred to as an innocent or physiologic murmur, is a type of heart murmur that arises due to physiological conditions outside the heart rather than structural abnormalities within the heart itself. It is important to note that serious medical conditions can still occur even in the absence of a primary heart defect. Peripheral factors can sometimes lead to abnormal findings in the heart, which is why the terms innocent or benign should be used with caution in this context. Innocent murmurs are generally harmless and tend to resolve as a child grows older. When performing a physical examination, the following characteristics of the murmur are typically observed: The murmur is soft, with an intensity of less than 3/6. However, it is important to understand that the intensity of a murmur does not necessarily correlate with the severity of any underlying structural heart disease, should it exist. The murmur is often position-dependent. It is commonly heard when the patient is lying supine and may disappear when the patient is upright or sitting. The murmur occurs during systole or may be continuous, spanning both systole and diastole. It is critical to recognize that murmurs occurring exclusively during diastole are always considered pathological. Physiologic splitting of the second heart sound (S2) may be present. There is no palpable thrill associated with the murmur.
